invert_y_hid.label: Invert Y Axis for HID mode
invert_y_hid.description: Invert the Y Axis when in HID mode, as some apps expect it to be inverted.

syncCalibrations.label: Sync calibrations across inputs
syncCalibrations.description: Syncronise calibrations across inputs that are used multiple times. For example if you have whammy on multiple profiles, turning this on will keep your whammy calibration syncronised, while turning it off means you can have different calibrations per profile.

xinput_on_windows.label: Use xinput instead of HID on windows
xinput_on_windows.description: Pick if you wish to have your controllers emulate an XInput device or an HID device when plugged into a Windows PC. Note that this setting has no effect on macOS, Linux or on game consoles.

ps4EmulationMode.label: Controller type on PS4/5
ps4EmulationMode.description: Pick the device type to emulate on PS4/5. PS3 works with Rock Band 4 without auth, but won't work in system menus or other games. PS4/5 works everywhere but requires authentication. For fortnite festival you can use a profile that emulates a keyboard to avoid needing auth.

legendMode.label: Icons to show
legendMode.description: Pick the icons to show below. This adjusts the icons and names shown in the UI, such as using A or B instead of Cross and Circle

cymbalGlitchFix.label: Apply the cymbal glitch fix
cymbalGlitchFix.description: Rock band 3 had a bug where hitting two cymbals at the same time would cause one of the cymbals to be dropped. This mitigates that bug, but may not work as well on Rock Band 2. This setting only applies on PS3 and Xbox 360.

device_to_emulate.label: Device to emulate
device_to_emulate.description: Pick the device to emulate. This is how you pick if your emulating a guitar or gamepad.

cycle.description: Cycling inputs let you jump between a set list of values. This can be useful for something like the pickup selector, where you could map a button to the pickup selector, and each time you press the button, it jumps between each notch.

getting_started.title: Getting started
getting_started.text: Put your Raspberry Pi Pico or Pico 2 into bootloader mode by holding BOOTSEL and connecting it to your pc, then download the following UF2 and drag it into the USB Drive named either RPI-RP2 for Pico 1 or RP2350 for Pico 2 that shows up. Once programmed, click Connect to Santroller and connect to the device.

face_button_mapping_mode.label: Face Button Mapping Mode
face_button_mapping_mode.description: Face buttons are in different positions on different controllers. For example, if you were to use a Wii Classic controller on an Xbox 360, label based mode will map A to A and B to B, while position based mode would swap A with B and X with Y.

assignments.title: Assignments
assignments.description: One of the key improvements with Santroller 2 is that you can have multiple profiles, but this means you need to tell Santroller 2 when you want your profiles used. Assignments are how this is done. Assignments come in two parts - one is the assignment itself, such as say assigning to plugging a Wii Guitar into a Wii Adapter, and the emulation type, such as USB or Bluetooth. This lets you do things like using different profiles for bluetooth vs for USB, but does mean you have to wrap your head around assignments.
assignments.specificConsoleDesc: Enable to apply this profile when plugged into a specific device, for example setting this to PS3 would only apply this profile when plugged into a PS3.
assignments.forcedTypeDesc: Enable to ignore console detection and always use a specific mode for this profile.
assignments.missingDevice: This profile is missing an emulation assignment. Without one, santroller doesn't know when it should use this profile, so it won't be used.
assignments.missing: This profile is missing an assignment! Without one, it won't ever be assigned
